claims.text: Directly deposited elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy substrates undergo Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion contributes to premature coating failure.
Depositing TiN at the Cr/Zr interface can produce a continuous, well-adherent interlayer.
The TiN interlayer acts as a physical diffusion barrier at the Cr/Zr interface.
The TiN barrier reduces atomic mobility at the Cr/Zr interface.
Reduced interfacial atomic mobility inhibits Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion prevents formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Cr–Zr intermetallic phases can degrade coating integrity during high-temperature exposure.
A TiN-barriered Cr coating will show significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than a directly deposited Cr coating.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will enhance coating integrity relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
The TiN-barriered system will sustain corrosion and oxidation protection during subcritical-water exposure at approximately 300–350°C.
The TiN-barriered system will sustain corrosion and oxidation protection during steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for tens of minutes to about one hour.
Subcritical-water exposure at approximately 300–350°C represents normal operating conditions for the proposed evaluation.
Steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for tens of minutes to about one hour represents accident-relevant conditions.
Direct Cr-coated zirconium-alloy substrates are prone to accelerated interdiffusion and premature failure in high-temperature steam.
Variations in TiN barrier quality and adhesion can influence coating performance.
